claims.text: What the strip looks like Type 1: an RBBB-like QRS in V1–V2 (sometimes V3) with a prominent J point and coved ST elevation that descends into an inverted T wave.
claims.quote: The type 1 Brugada ECG pattern has prominent J-point and ST elevation in V1 and V2 (sometimes involving V3) that causes the QRS complex in these leads to resemble right bundle branch block. The ST segment is coved and descends to an inverted T-wave.

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Type 1: coved ST elevation ≥ 2 mm in V1–V2 with T-wave inversion
claims.quote: Type 1: Coved ST elevation ≥ 2 mm in V1–V2 with T-wave inversion

claims.text: LITFL type 1: coved ST elevation > 2 mm in > 1 of V1–V3 followed by a negative T wave — the only potentially diagnostic ECG abnormality
claims.quote: Coved ST segment elevation >2mm in >1 of V1-V3 followed by a negative T wave. This is the only ECG abnormality that is potentially diagnostic.

claims.text: LITFL type 2: > 2 mm of saddleback-shaped ST elevation
claims.quote: Brugada Type 2 has >2mm of saddleback shaped ST elevation.

claims.text: Type 3: the morphology of type 1 or type 2 but with < 2 mm of ST elevation
claims.quote: Brugada type 3: can be the morphology of either type 1 or type 2, but with <2mm of ST segment elevation.

claims.text: Types 2 and 3 are not diagnostic; they may change to type 1 spontaneously, with fever, or with medications
claims.quote: Lesser degrees of these patterns (type 2 and type 3 Brugada ECG patterns) are not considered diagnostic. The type 2 and type 3 patterns may change to a type 1 pattern spontaneously, with fever, or in response to medications.

claims.text: Diagnosis needs this coved ECG pattern plus one clinical criterion: documented VF or polymorphic VT, family history of sudden cardiac death < 45 years, coved-type ECGs in family members, VT inducible on programmed electrical stimulation, syncope, or nocturnal agonal respiration
claims.quote: This ECG abnormality must be associated with one of the following clinical criteria to make the diagnosis: Documented ventricular fibrillation (VF) or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT). Family history of sudden cardiac death at <45 years old . Coved-type ECGs in family members. Inducibility of VT with programmed electrical stimulation . Syncope. Nocturnal agonal respiration.

claims.text: Unmasked by: the changes can be transient and can be unmasked or augmented by fever, ischemia, drugs (sodium channel blockers such as flecainide and propafenone, calcium channel blockers, alpha agonists, beta blockers, nitrates, cholinergic stimulation, cocaine, alcohol), hypokalemia, hyperkalemia, hypothermia, and DC cardioversion
claims.quote: ECG changes can be transient with Brugada syndrome and can also be unmasked or augmented by multiple factors: Fever Ischaemia Multiple Drugs Sodium channel blockers eg: Flecainide, Propafenone Calcium channel blockers Alpha agonists Beta Blockers Nitrates Cholinergic stimulation Cocaine Alcohol Hypokalaemia Hyperkalaemia Hypothermia Post DC cardioversion

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Associated with sudden cardiac death; a genetic sodium channel disorder (SCN5A)
claims.quote: Associated with sudden cardiac death; genetic sodium channel disorder (SCN5A)

claims.text: Mechanism: early loss of the action-potential plateau, especially in the epicardium of the RV outflow tract, giving the right precordial changes and a tendency to ventricular tachyarrhythmias; most mutations are in SCN5A (loss of inward sodium current)
claims.quote: These abnormalities lead to early loss of the action potential plateau, particularly in the epicardial cells of the right ventricular outflow tract that produce characteristic right precordial ECG changes and a propensity to ventricular tachyarrhythmias. Although different mutations have been reported, most are in the SCN5A gene, producing a loss-of-function of the inward sodium current

claims.text: Over 60 mutations described; at least 50% are spontaneous, but familial clustering and autosomal dominant inheritance occur
claims.quote: Over 60 different mutations have been described so far and at least 50% are spontaneous mutations, but familial clustering and autosomal dominant inheritance has been demonstrated.

claims.text: Most patients with clinically apparent Brugada syndrome are male (80 to 90%)
claims.quote: The majority of patients with clinically apparent Brugada syndrome are male (80 to 90%)

claims.text: Symptoms Most diagnosed patients are asymptomatic; in some it causes syncope or sudden cardiac death from polymorphic VT and VF, which can happen during sleep
claims.quote: The majority of patients diagnosed with Brugada syndrome are asymptomatic (1). However, in some patients it leads to syncope or sudden cardiac death due to polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation. Ventricular arrhythmias can cause sudden death during sleep.

claims.text: Events occur more often at night and usually not with exercise; fever and some medications (sodium channel blockers, beta-blockers, certain antidepressants and antipsychotics, lithium, alcohol, cocaine) can bring them on
claims.quote: Events occur more often at night and are not usually related to exercise. Events may also be brought on by fever and by certain medications, including sodium channel blockers, beta-blockers, certain antidepressants and antipsychotics, lithium, alcohol, and cocaine

claims.text: Treatment The only proven therapy is an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD); quinidine has been proposed where an ICD is unavailable or inappropriate (e.g., neonates)
claims.quote: The only proven therapy is an implantable cardioverter – defibrillator (ICD). Quinidine has been proposed as an alternative in settings where ICD’s are unavailable or where they would be inappropriate (eg: neonates).

claims.text: Genetic testing is usually recommended (yield about 20%)
claims.quote: Genetic testing is usually recommended and has a yield of approximately 20%

claims.text: Undiagnosed, its mortality has been estimated at 10% per year
claims.quote: Undiagnosed, Brugada syndrome has been estimated to have a mortality of 10% per year.
